You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your p4_pathway and
p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

# Outcome sub-dossier — Tallgrass Energy, LP realized record, ~3-5-year horizon (~2021-2023)

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. Tallgrass Energy, LP (formerly Tallgrass Energy
> GP, LP, CIK 0001633651) is the surviving public filer that continued after the 2018
> transaction; it was itself taken private in April 2020, before the fixed ~2021-2023
> outcome window began, so no post-closing 10-K exists inside that window. This
> sub-dossier contains no information about how the 2018 transaction was structured.

## Public-reporting status after the 2018 transaction, through going-private
- Tallgrass Energy, LP (CIK 0001633651, formerly named Tallgrass Energy GP, LP) filed
  annual reports on Form 10-K through fiscal year 2019, filed 2020-02-12. [SRC: SEC accession 0001633651-20-000013, Form 10-K]
- On December 16, 2019, Tallgrass Energy, LP ("TGE") entered an Agreement and Plan of
  Merger with Prairie Private Acquiror LP ("Buyer"), Prairie Merger Sub LLC, and TGE's
  general partner, providing for Buyer's affiliates to acquire the publicly held Class A
  Shares of TGE. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-20-110372, Form 8-K]
- The merger completed April 17, 2020 at 7:02 a.m. Central Time: TGE survived as a
  Delaware limited partnership; each outstanding Class A share (other than shares
  already held by the Prairie acquiror entities) was converted into $22.45 cash per
  share, with approximately $3.5 billion paid in aggregate as merger consideration. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-20-110372, Form 8-K]
- In connection with that closing, TGE requested the New York Stock Exchange remove its
  Class A Shares from listing (Form 25), and trading in the shares was suspended before
  the opening of trading on April 17, 2020. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-20-110372, Form 8-K]
- TGE filed a Form 15-12B on April 27, 2020 to terminate/suspend its Exchange Act
  reporting duty, certifying approximately 6 holders of record as of that date. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-20-120697, Form 15-12B]
- At the April 2020 closing, three independent directors (Roy N. Cook, Thomas A. Gerke,
  Terrance D. Towner) were removed from the board (stated not to result from any
  disagreement over operations/policies), five new directors were appointed, and five
  directors (William R. Moler, Wallace C. Henderson, Matthew J.K. Runkle, Guy G.
  Buckley, and Marcelino Oreja Arburúa) continued to serve; William R. Moler signed the
  closing Form 8-K as Chief Executive Officer. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-20-110372, Form 8-K]

## No public periodic record within the fixed ~2021-2023 window
- A search of Tallgrass Energy, LP's (CIK 0001633651) EDGAR filing history for annual
  reports finds no Form 10-K or Form 20-F filed after the FY2019 10-K; no periodic
  report covering fiscal years within the ~2021-2023 outcome window was located,
  consistent with the entity's deregistration in April 2020. [SRC: https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001633651&type=10-K]
- No source was found in which a parent or acquiror separately discloses this specific
  entity's or its pipeline segment's post-2020 financial trajectory for fiscal years
  2021-2023. [UNVERIFIED]

## Realized record under private ownership (press-sourced, imprecisely windowed)
- Under private ownership, the company (styled "Tallgrass") announced on May 18, 2022
  an agreement with ADM to capture and sequester carbon dioxide emissions from ADM's
  corn-processing complex in Columbus, Nebraska, transporting the CO2 to Tallgrass's
  Eastern Wyoming Sequestration Hub as part of a project to convert its existing
  Trailblazer natural gas pipeline to CO2 service. [SRC: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20220518005372/en/Tallgrass-to-Capture-and-Sequester-CO2-Emissions-From-ADM-Corn-Processing-Complex-in-Nebraska]
- This 2022 announcement falls within the fixed ~2021-2023 outcome window and indicates
  continued operating investment in the pipeline asset base rather than a disclosed
  divestiture or wind-down, but it is a press release, not an audited financial
  disclosure, and includes no company-wide financial scalar. [SRC: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20220518005372/en/Tallgrass-to-Capture-and-Sequester-CO2-Emissions-From-ADM-Corn-Processing-Complex-in-Nebraska]

## Items sought but not found
- No reputable-press or primary source was located reporting a bankruptcy, dissolution,
  goodwill/asset impairment, or divestiture of the core Tallgrass pipeline business
  specifically dated within the ~2021-2023 window. A Moody's rating action on the
  acquiring entity (Prairie ECI Acquiror LP) and an affirmation of Tallgrass Energy
  Partners, LP's notes rating were reported in December 2020, before the fixed window,
  and are not cited here as an in-window outcome fact. [UNVERIFIED]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- Tallgrass Energy, LP, the surviving public filer of the 2018 transaction, was itself
  acquired and taken private approximately 22 months after that transaction's closing,
  in an approximately $3.5 billion cash merger completed April 17, 2020, followed by
  removal from NYSE listing and deregistration under the Exchange Act. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-20-110372, Form 8-K; SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-20-120697, Form 15-12B]
- Because of that deregistration, there is no public audited outcome record (10-K/20-F)
  for the fixed ~2021-2023 window; the only in-window traceable fact is a 2022 press
  release describing continued investment in the pipeline asset base (a carbon-capture
  conversion project with ADM), with no divestiture, impairment, or bankruptcy located
  in-window. [SRC: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20220518005372/en/Tallgrass-to-Capture-and-Sequester-CO2-Emissions-From-ADM-Corn-Processing-Complex-in-Nebraska]
- Per the no-record convention, this case is coded **uncertain** on the fixed-window
  financial outcome: the absence of a public periodic-reporting record after April 2020
  precludes a sourced determination of the realized 3-5-year trajectory of the acquired
  business under private ownership.

[SLICE END]
